definition_zh: 机场；航空站；空港；机场的
definition_en: a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for travellers
core_image: 跑道上飞机正滑向航站楼
scene: 跑道旁，一架飞机正滑向航站楼。Our plane landed at the airport on time.
sceneCN: 这里 airport 是「机场」（第 1 个义项：飞机起降的场所）；句意为我们的飞机准时降落在机场。

senses.title: The place for flights
senses.definition: the whole place where aircraft arrive and leave
senses.definitionCN: 飞机抵达与离开的整个场所
senses.example: Our plane landed at the airport on time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的飞机准时降落在机场。
senses.why: Air plus port moves a harbour into the sky: the place where aircraft come and go.
senses.whyCN: air 加 port，把港口搬到天上，就是飞机起降的场所。

senses.title: The terminal buildings
senses.definition: the buildings where travellers check in and wait
senses.definitionCN: 旅客办手续与等候的建筑物
senses.example: The airport was full of holiday crowds.
senses.exampleCN: 航站楼里挤满了度假的人群。
senses.why: Travellers meet the place through its halls, so the buildings themselves are called the airport.
senses.whyCN: 旅客接触这个场所主要通过大厅，所以建筑群本身也被叫作 airport。

senses.title: A small airfield
senses.definition: a modest field with simple buildings for light planes
senses.definitionCN: 供轻型飞机使用、建筑简单的场地
senses.example: A small airport serves the island.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小型航空站为这个岛服务。
senses.why: The same name is used for a field with only simple buildings.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名称也用在只有简单建筑的场地。

items.en: English port first named a harbour where ships came and went.
items.cn: 英语 port 最初指船只往来的港口。

items.en: Air named the open sky above the ground.
items.cn: air 指地面之上的开阔天空。

items.en: When planes began to fly, English joined the two words for a field with buildings.
items.cn: 飞机开始飞行后，英语把这两个词结合起来，指带建筑的场地。

items.en: Today it covers terminals, runways and the whole travel stop.

definition_en: a warning sound or device, or the fear it causes, or to make someone afraid
core_image: 清晨闹钟突然响起来
scene: 清晨，床头的闹钟突然响了起来。The alarm woke the whole family.
sceneCN: 这里 alarm 是「闹钟」（第 2 个义项：按时叫醒人的钟）；句意为闹钟吵醒了全家。

senses.title: A warning sound
senses.definition: a loud sound that warns of danger
senses.definitionCN: 提醒危险的大声响
senses.example: The fire alarm rang at noon.
senses.why: The Italian cry to arms became a sudden warning sound.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语「拿起武器」的呼喊，变成突然示警的声响。

senses.title: A waking clock
senses.definition: a clock that makes a sound at a set time
senses.definitionCN: 在设定时间发出声响的钟
senses.example: My alarm goes off at six.
senses.why: A clock that warns a sleeper to wake up borrowed the name of the warning.
senses.whyCN: 提醒睡眠者醒来的钟，借用了「示警」的名称。

senses.title: A sudden fear
senses.definition: the fear felt when danger appears
senses.definitionCN: 危险出现时感到的恐惧
senses.example: She jumped up in alarm.
senses.why: The warning lands in the mind as fear, which gives the feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 警报落进心里就成了恐惧，因此有了表示感受的义项。

senses.title: To frighten someone
senses.definition: to make a person feel sudden fear
senses.definitionCN: 使人突然感到害怕
senses.example: The smoke alarmed the neighbours.
senses.why: Putting the warning into other people is the verb sense of making them afraid.
senses.whyCN: 把警报放进别人心里，就是动词「使惊恐」。

definition_en: living and not dead, or full of energy, or still in use, or full of something
core_image: 清早的操场上有人跑步呼吸
scene: 清晨的操场上，几个人在跑步，呼吸有力。The old tree is still alive.

senses.title: Living, not dead
senses.definition: having life and not being dead
senses.definitionCN: 拥有生命而不是死亡
senses.example: The fish was still alive.
senses.why: The old phrase on life meant being in life, so alive first says that life is still there.
senses.whyCN: 古短语 on life 意为处在生命之中，所以 alive 首先表示生命仍在。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: showing quick energy and interest
senses.definitionCN: 表现出充沛的精力与兴趣
senses.example: The class came alive after the game.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏之后全班活跃起来。
senses.why: A living body moves and reacts, so being alive also pictures energy in action.
senses.whyCN: 活着的身体会动会反应，所以 alive 也画出行动中的活力。

senses.title: Still existing
senses.definition: kept in use or in memory
senses.definitionCN: 仍被使用或仍被记住
senses.example: The old custom is still alive.
senses.why: A custom that has not died out is pictured as still having life.
senses.whyCN: 没有消失的习俗被画成「仍然有生命」。

senses.title: Full of living things
senses.definition: full of moving things, used in alive with
senses.definitionCN: 满是活动的东西，用于 alive with
senses.example: The pond was alive with fish.
senses.why: A place crowded with moving creatures looks as if life fills it.
senses.whyCN: 一个充满游动生物的地方，看起来就像被生命填满。

definition_en: every one of a group, or the whole of something, or completely

sceneCN: 这里 all 是「全部」（第 1 个义项：一个群体中的每一个）；句意为所有学生都举起了手。

senses.title: Every member of a group
senses.definition: each person or thing in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的每个人或物
senses.example: All the students stood up.
senses.why: The old word named a whole group, and naming the whole means touching every member.
senses.whyCN: 古词指一个完整的群体，说整体就等于说到每一个成员。

senses.title: The whole of something
senses.definition: the complete amount or extent of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物的全部数量或范围
senses.example: He drank all the water.
senses.why: From a group of people the word widened to any complete amount, such as all the water.
senses.whyCN: 从一群人扩大到任何完整的数量，就像 all the water。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: entirely, with nothing left out
senses.definitionCN: 整个地，没有剩下
senses.example: The floor was all wet.
senses.why: A whole with nothing left out becomes the adverb sense of completely.
senses.whyCN: 整体不剩一点，就变成副词「完全地」。

senses.title: The only thing
senses.definition: the single thing, with nothing else
senses.definitionCN: 唯一的事物，没有别的
senses.example: All she wants is a quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 她只想要一个安静的房间。
senses.why: The whole can shrink to one thing when nothing else is mentioned, which gives the sense of only.
senses.whyCN: 当没有别的被提到，整体就缩成一件东西，于是有「唯一」的意思。

definition_en: to let something happen, or to give time or money for a purpose

senses.definition: to let a person do something

senses.whyCN: 法语动词意为准许，所以让某人做某事就是第一义。

senses.title: To let something happen
senses.definition: to make it possible for an event to take place
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事得以发生
senses.example: The open window allowed fresh air in.
senses.exampleCN: 开着的窗让新鲜空气进来。
senses.why: The same granting was widened from people to events and things.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「准许」从人扩展到事件与事物。

senses.title: To set aside time or money
senses.definition: to plan an amount of time or money for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个用途计划出时间或钱
senses.example: Allow an hour for the journey.
senses.why: Granting a share of one's time or money is the planning sense of allowing.
senses.whyCN: 从自己的时间或钱里让出一份，就是安排上的留出。

senses.title: To take into account
senses.definition: to think about something when making a plan
senses.definitionCN: 做计划时把某事考虑进去
senses.example: Allow for the wind on the hill.
senses.why: Making room in a plan for a difficulty is the phrase allow for.
senses.whyCN: 在计划里为困难让出空间，就是 allow for。

senses.whyCN: 把「只有一个」放在名词后加以突出，就得到「仅仅」。

senses.title: Feeling lonely

definition_zh: 在……之中；在……中间；其中之一
definition_en: in the middle of a group, or surrounded by things, or one of a number
core_image: 一群学生中间站着新来的同学
scene: 一群学生中间站着一位新来的同学。A new pupil stood among the students.
sceneCN: 这里 among 是「在……之中」（第 1 个义项：处在群体内部）；句意为一位新同学站在学生们中间。

senses.title: Inside a group of people
senses.definition: in the middle of a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 处在一群人的中间
senses.example: A new pupil stood among the students.
senses.exampleCN: 一位新同学站在学生们中间。
senses.why: The old word meant in the crowd, so being inside a group is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词意为「在人群中」，所以处在群体内部是第一义。

senses.title: Surrounded by things
senses.definition: surrounded by things on all sides
senses.definitionCN: 四周都被事物围住
senses.example: A small house stands among the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小房子坐落在树丛中。
senses.why: The crowd was replaced by objects, and being inside a crowd became being surrounded by things.
senses.whyCN: 人群换成物体，「在人群里」就变成四周被事物包围。

senses.title: One of a number
senses.definition: included in a set as one member
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个成员被包含在一组里
senses.example: He is one among many young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他是众多年轻作家中的一位。
senses.why: The same inside position marks a member counted with the rest, which gives the sense of one of a number.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「在里面」的位置标记被数在其中的成员，这就是其中之一。

senses.definition: belonging to a period of history long before our own

senses.why: Ante meant before, so the word first marks a whole age that lies before ours.

senses.title: Very old in itself
senses.definition: having existed for a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 自身已经存在了很久
senses.example: An ancient tree stands by the gate.
senses.why: The long stretch of time was transferred from an age to a single thing that has lasted.
senses.whyCN: 把漫长的时间从整个时代转到一件存留很久的事物上，就是古老的。

senses.title: Worn by many years

senses.example: The ancient walls are still standing.
senses.why: When the years are visible in the stone itself, the word describes the wear of age.

senses.title: Joining two things
senses.definition: used to join two words or groups of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个同类词或词组
senses.example: She bought bread and milk.
senses.why: The word puts one thing beside another, so joining two of the same kind is its first use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一物放到另一物旁边，所以连接两个同类项是第一用法。

senses.title: Joining actions in order
senses.definition: used to join two actions that follow each other
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个先后发生的动作
senses.example: He sat down and opened the book.
senses.why: The old sense of then survives when two actions are placed one after the other.
senses.whyCN: 当两个动作一件接一件排放时，古老的「然后」义就保留下来。

senses.title: Joining a cause and a result
senses.definition: used to join a cause with what follows from it
senses.definitionCN: 连接原因与由此产生的结果
senses.example: It began to rain and we went home.
senses.exampleCN: 开始下雨，于是我们回家了。
senses.why: Placing a result right after its cause gives the sense of so or therefore.
senses.whyCN: 把结果紧接在原因后面，就得到「于是、因此」。

normal.en: The old root meant narrow: anger is a mind squeezed tight by displeasure.
normal.cn: 古词根意为狭窄：愤怒就是心里被不快挤紧。

normal.en: The same family also gives anger and angrily.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 anger 与 angrily。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase angry with.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「对某人生气」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of angry in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 angry 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: feeling strong displeasure about something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「生气的」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a boy clenching his fist at a broken model.
abstract.cn: 想象男孩握紧拳头盯着被弄坏的模型。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She was angry about the broken window.
examples.cn: 她为被打破的窗子生气。

examples.en: The crowd grew angry at the delay.
examples.cn: 人群因延误而愤怒起来。

examples.en: He gave her an angry look.

root: angry 来自古诺尔斯语 angr「悲伤、烦恼」，同一词根还带有狭窄紧绷的意味；中古英语用它形容满心不快的人，十四世纪同时保留悲伤与激烈两种意味，今天通常指对某人或某事感到不快。

definition_en: a living creature that can move and feel, or a beast other than a human, or relating to such creatures
core_image: 草地上奔跑的鹿群
scene: 草地上，一群鹿正奔跑而过。The deer is a wild animal.
sceneCN: 这里 animal 是「动物」（第 1 个义项：会活动会呼吸的生物）；句意为鹿是一种野生动物。

senses.title: A living creature
senses.definition: a living thing that can move and feel
senses.definitionCN: 能活动、能感知的生物
senses.example: The deer is a wild animal.
senses.why: Anima meant breath, and a breathing, moving creature is the first sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: anima 意为气息，会呼吸、会活动的生物就是这个词的第一义。

senses.title: A beast other than a human
senses.definition: a creature other than a human being
senses.definitionCN: 人以外的生物
senses.example: Food is needed by humans and animals alike.
senses.why: When humans are set apart, the same word marks the other breathing creatures.
senses.whyCN: 当人把人自己分开说，同一个词就标记其余会呼吸的生物。

senses.title: Relating to such creatures
senses.definition: used before a noun for things that come from or concern creatures
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指来自或关于这类生物的
senses.example: Animal fat is used in some soap.
senses.exampleCN: 有些肥皂使用动物脂肪。
senses.why: Putting the creature before a noun turns it into a describing word.
senses.whyCN: 把这类生物放在名词前，就变成形容词用法。

intro.en: The recorded history of animal is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 animal 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Anima meant breath, air or soul.
items.cn: anima 意为气息、空气或灵魂。

items.en: Animalis meant living, having breath.
items.cn: animalis 意为活着的、有气息的。

items.en: English borrowed animal for a living creature that moves.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入 animal，指能活动的生物。

items.en: Later it often marked beasts as distinct from people.
items.cn: 后来它常把人以外的兽类与人区分开。

items.en: Today words such as wildlife and animal food are common.
items.cn: 今天 wildlife 与 animal food 这类词很常见。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: A general word for any living being.

An animal kept at home for company.
entries.definitionCN: 指养在家中作伴的动物。
